title: FFmpeg
subtitle: FFmpeg frames a headless Linux desktop as H.264 for screen sharing into Teams meetings and drives the media studio's transforms.
lede: Helix needed a way for the digital employee to show its work in a Teams meeting. I decided it should share a real screen: a headless Linux desktop with a virtual display, a window manager, Chromium and a terminal, captured by FFmpeg's X11 grabber and encoded to H.264. I tuned the encoder for slides and terminal text, and for the viewer who joins late. FFmpeg serves the raw H.264 stream on a local socket. The Rust voice engine frames each access unit into a small versioned contract and hands it to the Windows media bridge, which publishes it into the call as Teams screen sharing.
quote: I treat an agent-facing tool as an attack surface first and a convenience second.
evidence: Video encoding for screen sharing: a headless Linux desktop encoded to H.264 for slides and terminal text and for late joiners, shared into Teams meetings.
Sandboxing agent tools: a fixed menu of typed media transforms whose FFmpeg arguments are written by code, with no codec, filter or shell text accepted from the agent.
Cross-host file delivery: inputs staged onto the machine that runs the job and outputs hash-checked at the destination.
author: Corey James
